title: Fire Alarm Delay Can't Stop a Record-Smashing Swim Morning!
summary:
Imagine you're about to dive into a big race, and suddenly a fire alarm goes off! That's what happened at the Junior Pan Pacific Championships in Vancouver, Canada. The start was delayed by 30 minutes while everyone made sure it was safe. But once the splashing started, the excitement was huge!

This meet is extra special because it's the first time they're swimming the 50-meter butterfly (a super-fast stroke where both arms move together). In the girls' race, American Gabi Brito was the top seed by just 0.01 seconds over Australia's Olivia Hine. That's faster than a blink! In the morning swim, Brito touched the wall first in 26.45 seconds. That's now the meet record, which means she's the fastest ever at this event. Olivia Hine was right behind at 26.73, and she actually held the record for a few minutes until Brito swam in the next heat. Talk about a close race!

Another American, Kennedi Southern, came in third at 26.80. Canada had two swimmers make the top final too: Helena Tripp and Rowan Baglole. But here's a cool rule: only two swimmers from each country can go to the 'A' final (the big one at night). So even though American Mia Buff swam fast enough, she had to go to the 'B' final. That meant 14-year-old Victoria Fernanda Garcia Caldera from Mexico got bumped up to the 'A' final with her time of 27.43. She must be so excited!

In the boys' 200 freestyle, American Abi Burke was the only one to go under 2 minutes, swimming 1:59.23. That's like swimming four laps of a pool in less time than it takes to brush your teeth really well! She's the favorite for tonight's final. Australian Jodie Mead got a personal best of 2:00.29, and Japan's Haruno Tanimoto was third at 2:00.52.

All eyes are also on 17-year-old American Luka Mijatovic, who is swimming two tough races today: the 200 free and the 800 free. He's the top seed in both, which means he's expected to win. Can he do it? We'll find out tonight!
why_it_matters: It shows that even when an unexpected event like a fire alarm interrupts your plans, you can stay focused and still achieve something great.

background_read: The Junior Pan Pacific Championships bring together young swimmers from countries around the Pacific Ocean.
The meet is held in Vancouver, a city on the west coast of Canada.
In swimming, a meet record means the fastest time ever swum at that competition.
Article_Structure: WHO: Swimmers from the United States, Australia, Canada, Mexico, and Japan, including Gabi Brito and Luka Mijatovic.
WHAT: A fire alarm delayed the morning swim by 30 minutes, then Gabi Brito set a meet record in the 50-meter butterfly and Abi Burke led the boys' 200 freestyle.
WHERE: At the Junior Pan Pacific Championships in Vancouver, Canada.
WHY: Because swimmers were competing in heats to earn spots in the night 'A' final, and the meet included the first 50-meter butterfly races.

perspectives.description: They felt excited to see close races and a meet record despite the scary fire alarm delay.
